query: SELECT * FROM duckdb_functions() WHERE database_name='code' ORDER BY schema_name,function_name
rows: Number of function/method definitions for the given language

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Count the function and method definitions in a source string for a given language, using tree-sitter to find definition nodes. Returns NULL when the source or language is NULL; an unknown language id is a clear error. Use it as a quick structural metric of how many functions a file defines.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Number of function/method definitions for a language, e.g. `count_functions(src, 'python')` → `2`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Count function/method definitions in the source (→ 2).","sql":"SELECT code.main.count_functions('def a(): pass\ndef b(): pass\n', 'python');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Count Function Definitions

rows: Total number of physical lines in the source (NULL → NULL)

rows.vgi.doc_llm:
Count the total number of physical lines in a source string, including blank and comment lines. Language-agnostic (no parsing). A single trailing newline is NOT counted as an extra line, so 'a
b
' and 'a
b' both report 2; an empty string reports 0. Returns NULL when the source is NULL. Use it for raw file-size / line-count metrics.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Total physical lines in the source, e.g. `count_lines('a\nb\n')` → `2`. NULL in → NULL.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Count the physical lines in a source string (→ 2).","sql":"SELECT code.main.count_lines('fn a() {}\nfn b() {}\n');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Count Physical Lines

rows: Comment texts in the source, as a VARCHAR[]

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Extract the comment texts (line and block comments) from a source string for a given language, returned as a `VARCHAR[]`. NULL source or language → NULL list; empty source → empty list; an unknown language is a clear error. Use it to mine documentation, TODOs, or license headers.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Collect the comment texts from Rust source as a VARCHAR[].","sql":"SELECT code.main.extract_comments('// header\nfn a() {}\n', 'rust');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Extract Comment Texts

rows: Import / use / require statements in the source, as a VARCHAR[]

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Extract the import / use / require statements from a source string for a given language, returned as a `VARCHAR[]` of the statement texts. NULL source or language → NULL list; an empty source → empty list; an unknown language is a clear error. Use it to discover a file's dependencies.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Extract each import statement from Python source, one per row.","sql":"SELECT UNNEST(code.main.extract_imports('import os\nimport sys\n', 'python'));"}]
rows.vgi.title: Extract Import Statements

rows: String-literal texts in the source, as a VARCHAR[]

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Extract the string-literal texts from a source string for a given language, returned as a `VARCHAR[]` (the literals including their quotes). NULL source or language → NULL list; empty source → empty list; an unknown language is a clear error. Use it to find hard-coded strings, secrets, or URLs.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Collect the string-literal texts from Rust source as a VARCHAR[].","sql":"SELECT code.main.extract_strings('let s = \"hello\";\n', 'rust');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Extract String Literals

rows: Infer the source language from a filename's extension (NULL if unknown)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Infer the programming language of a file from its name or path extension, e.g. 'src/main.rs' → 'rust', 'app.py' → 'python'. Returns NULL when the filename is NULL or its extension maps to no supported language. Use it to route files to the right language id for the other functions.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Infer a file's language from its extension, e.g. `language_of('main.rs')` → `'rust'`. NULL if unknown.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Detect the source language of a file from its extension (→ 'rust').","sql":"SELECT code.main.language_of('src/main.rs');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Detect Source Language

rows: Lines of code: non-blank, non-comment lines for the given language

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Count the lines of code (LOC) in a source string for a given language: physical lines that are neither blank nor purely comments. Returns NULL when the source or language is NULL; an unknown language id is a clear error. Use it for code-size metrics that ignore whitespace and comments.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Non-blank, non-comment lines for a language, e.g. `loc(src, 'rust')`. NULL in → NULL; unknown language errors.
rows.vgi.keywords: ["lines of code","loc","sloc","code metrics","non-comment lines","effective lines","source lines"]
rows.vgi.title: Lines Of Code

rows: List the language ids this worker can parse

rows.vgi.doc_llm: List every language id this worker can parse, one per row. These are the exact values accepted as the `language` argument by language_of, loc, count_functions, the extract_* functions, ts_query, symbols and ts_nodes. Use it to discover which languages are available.
rows.vgi.doc_md: List the language ids this worker can parse. Column: `language`.
rows.vgi.title: Supported Languages Catalog

rows: Structural symbols (functions, classes, methods, structs, enums, …) of a source doc

rows.vgi.doc_llm: List the structural symbols of one source document — functions, methods, classes, structs, enums, interfaces and traits — one row each, ordered by start line, with their kind, name and 1-based line span. `source` and `language` are bind-time constants. NULL source → no rows; malformed source is best-effort (tree-sitter recovers); an unknown language is a clear error. Use it to outline or index a file's definitions.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Structural symbols of a source doc as `(kind, name, start_line, end_line)` rows, e.g. `symbols('fn a() {}', 'rust')`.
rows.vgi.title: Source Symbols Listing

rows: Tree-sitter query matches over a source doc as (seq, capture, text, start_line, end_line) rows

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Run a tree-sitter S-expression query over one source document and return every capture as a row: a document-order sequence number, the capture name, the captured node's text, and its 1-based line span. `source`, `language` and `query` are bind-time constants. NULL source → no rows; an unknown language or malformed query is a clear error. The table-shaped counterpart to ts_query, for rich structural extraction.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Tree-sitter query captures as `(seq, capture, text, start_line, end_line)` rows, e.g. `ts_nodes(src, 'rust', '(function_item) @f')`.
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema:
[
  {"name":"seq","type":"BIGINT","description":"0-based capture index in document order."},
  {"name":"capture","type":"VARCHAR","description":"The query capture name (the @name in the tree-sitter query)."},
  {"name":"text","type":"VARCHAR","description":"The captured node's source text."},
  {"name":"start_line","type":"INTEGER","description":"1-based line where the captured node starts."},
  {"name":"end_line","type":"INTEGER","description":"1-based line where the captured node ends."}
]
rows.vgi.title: Tree-Sitter Query Nodes

rows: Run a tree-sitter query over the source and return the captured node texts (`VARCHAR[]`)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Run an arbitrary tree-sitter S-expression query over a source string for a given language and return every captured node's text as a `VARCHAR[]`. The power feature for ad-hoc structural search. NULL source/language/query → NULL list; an unknown language or a malformed query is a clear error.
rows.vgi.doc_md: Run a tree-sitter query and return captured node texts as a `VARCHAR[]`, e.g. `ts_query(src, 'rust', '(function_item name: (identifier) @n)')`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description":"Run a tree-sitter query and return captured node texts (here, the two function names).","sql":"SELECT code.main.ts_query('fn alpha() {}\nfn beta() {}\n', 'rust', '(function_item name: (identifier) @n)');"}]
rows.vgi.title: Run Tree-Sitter Query
